description: L2 reading points: JSP catalog entries and foundational readings, each an instance of an L1 specification.

excluded_generalizations: 1 + 1 = 2 in ℤ, ℚ or ℝ: the same numeral reading under a separate specification.
readings.notes: Five layers kept apart: mathematical statement (statement.math); Lean declaration (statement.lean_name, statement.lean); proof term (statement.proof_term); kernel verification (EV-0001); generalization (SPEC-nat-add-one via LIFT-0001).

catalog.title: Twin prime conjecture
catalog.text: Are there infinitely many pairs of primes differing by exactly two?

statement.math: There are infinitely many primes p with p + 2 prime.

lean.name: Survey.PrimeBridges.InfinitelyManyTwinPrimes
lean.note: Same body as statement.lean; compiled in EV-0004

leading_constraints: The shift set {0, 2} is admissible: the residue 1 avoids both shifts modulo every prime.
excluded_generalizations: Every even gap (Polignac; the content of DHL[2, 2]).
readings.notes: The reading's statement is compiled as Survey.PrimeBridges.InfinitelyManyTwinPrimes, and LIFT-009-3 (kernel-checked) shows it equivalent to BGP212.Gap.H1Le 2. The conjecture itself stays open.

catalog.title: Dickson conjecture
catalog.text: Do finitely many integer linear polynomials with positive leading coefficients take prime values simultaneously infinitely often whenever no fixed prime divisor obstructs this?

parameters.fs: every finite set of linear forms with positive leading coefficients and no fixed prime divisor

statement.math: Every such set of linear forms is simultaneously prime at infinitely many natural numbers.
statement.lean: def JSP_000029 : Prop := ∀ fs : Finset ℤ[X], (∀ f ∈ fs, f.degree = 1 ∧ 0 < f.leadingCoeff) → SchinzelCondition fs → {n : ℕ | ∀ f ∈ fs, (f.eval (n : ℤ)).natAbs.Prime}.Infinite

catalog.title: Consecutive prime gap bound of 186
catalog.text: Are there infinitely many consecutive prime pairs with gap at most 186? This is a quantitative bounded-prime-gaps problem.

statement.math: Infinitely many consecutive primes differ by at most 186.

excluded_generalizations: Other values of D, including lean-bgp212's target D = 212.

statement.math: For any real separation function F, the uniform target-fiber conditional mean of crossTalk F equals zero, on the finite Boolean pattern product space.

leading_constraints: Finite neuron and memory types with decidable equality; patterns range over a finite Boolean product; fixed target coordinate fiber.
The statement holds for arbitrary F : ℝ → ℝ.
excluded_generalizations: Does not imply zero variance, Gaussian error estimates, or retrieval capacity.
readings.notes: CP6c.1 and CP6c.2 are reported as kernel verified by the DAM repository, not independently survey verified. CP6c.3 is open.

statement.math: The conditional target-fiber average of the one-flip energy gap for polyF n equals the exact signal N^n − (N−2)^n, for every n.

leading_constraints: Polynomial separation polyF n, finite Boolean pattern model, uniform target fiber.
Exact finite identity; no asymptotic size regime.
excluded_generalizations: Does not establish the large-N approximation, error probability, variance, or capacity scaling.
readings.notes: CP6c.1 and CP6c.2 are reported as kernel verified by the DAM repository, not independently survey verified. CP6c.3 is open.

origin.title: Finite second moment of the one-flip noise

statement.math: Determine and prove the exact finite conditional second moment (and resulting variance) of the noise/cross-talk term under the DAM finite uniform pattern model.

leading_constraints: Target-fiber conditional averaging over a finite Boolean product model.
Define the exact second-moment expression and account for repeated-index correlations.
excluded_generalizations: No claimed Lean proof, Gaussian approximation, or capacity theorem.
readings.notes: CP6c.1 and CP6c.2 are reported as kernel verified by the DAM repository, not independently survey verified. CP6c.3 is open.
